prompt/zero: A pretrained model continues whatever text it is given. So write a task as text: an instruction, English to French, then a new input, cheese, and an arrow.
prompt/few: Better still, show it a few solved examples first: dog becomes chien, cow becomes vache.
prompt/answer: Now the likeliest continuation is fromage. The model picked up the task from examples in its context: in-context learning.
prompt/shots: With no examples, the prompt is zero-shot. One example makes it one-shot, and several make it few-shot.
frozen/frozen: No gradient step happened. The model only ran forward, and every weight is exactly what it was before.
frozen/tokens: The examples are just tokens in the context. Attention reads them like any earlier tokens, and to predict what follows such a pattern, the model has to work out the task.
frozen/gone: So nothing is kept. Send a new prompt without the examples, and the model starts from the same weights, with no trace of them.
frozen/cost: They do cost room in the context. An instruction of five tokens, two examples of four, and an input of three make sixteen tokens to read before the answer.
